correctness.rationale: Beta-weighted monomial moments produce coefficients O(k^{-alpha-1}); the twice-differentiated angular series is absolutely uniform for alpha>2. At the four roots of unity, first and alternating Fourier vectors diagonalize the exact 4×4 circulant Hessian; only rotation is in its kernel. Root-of-unity filters give the positive integral eigenvalues lambda1=4(alpha+1)∫(1-t)^alpha[A+B]dt and lambda2=8(alpha+1)∫(1-t)^alpha Bdt. Their difference uses F=(alpha+1)∫(1-t)^alpha(A−B)dt. The rational ratio B/A=4t(1+t)^4/(1+t²)^3 is strictly increasing from zero to eight, hence A−B has one sign change; a monotone likelihood-ratio argument proves at most one zero of F. Exact partial fractions give F(2)=24log2−12−3pi/2<0 and F(3)=120log2+6pi−102>0, establishing existence. Fresh independent exact symbolic differentiation verified R’/R=(1−t)(t²+6t+1)/(t(1+t)(1+t²)); numerical integrals independently checked both endpoint expressions and root 2.727841735934682. The second-variation Taylor formula yields the claimed sharp local quotient coefficient. The alpha=2 integral is used only for a continuous endpoint sign, not a Hessian at alpha=2.
residual_risks: The critical exponent is numerically approximated, exact uniqueness is analytical; no global quantitative stability result or alpha=2 twice-differentiability assertion.

value.rationale: For a classical regular-polygon minimizer in weighted Bergman energy, the local curvature determines sensitivity to perturbations beyond the binary global-minimum statement. Four poles are the first equispaced configuration with two distinct nonrotational real Fourier symmetry classes. Their unique soft-mode switch and one isotropic exponent are a sharp natural spectral phase classification with exact stability coefficient and rigorously identified transition, not a mere normalization or known minimum restatement.
residual_risks: Only local near-equilibrium Hessian stability for exactly four poles; no global quantitative minimizer stability claim.

final_claim: For four unit-strength poles at quarter-circle angles, in the normalized power-weighted Bergman L² energy and each alpha>2, the transverse Hessian has a positive double Fourier eigenvalue lambda1 and a positive single alternating-mode eigenvalue lambda2. Their difference 4F(alpha) changes sign exactly once at alpha*=2.72784173593468... in (2,3), producing unique isotropy of the three-dimensional rotational quotient and a sharp local stability coefficient one-half the smaller eigenvalue. No global stability bound or alpha=2 Hessian is claimed.
limitations: alpha>2 needed for series Hessian justification; alpha=2 is only F endpoint.
